sections.title: Some apples, some pears
sections.content: A plural object has two endings: the plural *-k* first, then the object ending. After *k* the object ending is *-at* or *-et*, chosen by vowel harmony: *alma → almák → almákat*, *körte → körték → körtéket*. After a consonant the plural takes its linking vowel first: *banán → banánok → banánokat*. Use this when you mean several of something without a number: *Almákat kérek.* (I'd like some apples.)
After a number or *kiló* the noun stays singular, so there is no *-k*: *három banánt*, *két kiló körtét*. Add *-kat / -ket* only when there is no number and you mean "some".
